rule: RB 9.3.1: a patrol Fighter requires a screening force for entering ships to continue

mutations_caught.no fighter barrier: Ships sailed on past a patrol fighter without a screen, or could not stop
mutations_caught.no stop option: Ships sailed on past a patrol fighter without a screen, or could not stop
mutations_caught.let-pass mark ignored: The ship sailing on did not reach its destination past the fighter
mutations_caught.barrier at the route end: A route ending beside the fighter was asked for a screen or a battle
mutations_caught.any patrol plane bars: A patrol bomber barred the ships' way after its single round
mutations_caught.stopping keeps movement: A ship that stopped beside the fighter could still sail on without a screen
mutations_caught.route end keeps movement: Ships that ended their route beside the fighter could sail on later without a screen
mutations_caught.any patrol plane ends the voyage: Ships that met a patrol bomber could not sail on later

seed_7193: Decision 724: a captured KMT naval transport leaving port into P14, bound for P32, met the Japanese fighter on patrol there, which fought its single round. Random play added the transport to a screen, then stopped instead (naval_screen_stop_route). Before endVoyage it then began a second voyage to P32 and P41; now it can only attack in place, which it did with a torpedo boat destroyer. In the Combat Phase the fighter accepted (naval_patrol_engage) and Japan scrambled a battleship and a torpedo boat destroyer from the Rehe major port.
